a.summary: The HTTP-body section's present-tense description still says the corpus has 14 seeds, but the same patch adds a 15th (gzip_folded_encoding) — and the patch edited that very sentence.
a.failure_scenario: A maintainer reading the only live description of the httpBody corpus counts 14, runs `ls` and gets 15, and cannot tell whether a seed was added without a notes update or whether one is uncommitted/spurious — exactly the corpus-rot question the section exists to answer. The F02 relabel was applied to the sentence while the number it contains was left wrong by the same patch.

b.summary: The httpBody seed count was left at 14 while the patch adds a 15th seed, and the same section now states 15 two paragraphs later.
b.failure_scenario: A reader (or the next agent auditing the corpus) reads line 1066, expects 14 seeds, counts 15 on disk, and cannot tell whether an uncommitted seed leaked in or the note is stale — the same document asserts both 14 and 15 for the same corpus.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
